text: It is 1987 and you are on a ferry from Belgium to England. Suddenly, the ferry starts tilting and water begins to pour in. You and many other passengers are trying to get to the deck by a rope ladder. You climb up the ladder and stand on the deck, looking at the 20 other passengers making their way up behind you. Directly below you, a man who is midway up the ladder seems frozen into immobility by fear or cold and is blocking the way. You try to speak and reach to him, but he does not react. People behind you are jostling. The ship seems to be sinking fast and the man is still blocking the ladder. You have a gun in your possession. From the crowd below, someone shouts that you should shoot the man to make him fall off. If you shoot the man, he will probably die, but the 20 other people will be able to climb on deck. If you do not shoot the man, he will probably continue blocking the way so that many of the people behind you will not be able to get on deck and therefore will drown.
